newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF MONACO V PSG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF MONACO V PSG.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Monaco and Paris St Germain who meet in the French first division on Sunday (1945 GMT).

Playing style: At home, Monaco usually line up with three in defence, Patrick Blondeau who has just been called into the France squad for the first time, captain Franck Dumas and youngster Martin Djetou. In midfield, which could be four or five strong, strongman Emmanuel Petit and Belgian creative force Enzo Scifo are both back after injury. But the most influential midfelder this season is Ali Benarbia behind a two-man attack of Brazilian Anderson and Nigeria's Victor Ikpeba, or three if brilliant teenager Thierry Henry is included.

Strengths: The strongest squad in the French league, which has helped Monaco make light of injury to several first choice players. Variety of scoring options with Anderson on 11 league goals and both Ikpeba and Henry on eight. A coach, Jean Tigana, strong on motivation who has also guided Monaco into the UEFA Cup quarter-finals with some brilliant counter-attacking football in the away legs.

Weaknesses: Small home crowds that create little atmosphere at Monaco's Louis II stadium. A pitch that has been almost unplayable in the cold, wet winter weeks -- despite dominating Cannes in their Cote d'Azur derby last month they only just won the match 1-0 with a late goal.

Motivation: A sixth league title and first since 1988, when they triumphed under Arsene Wenger. They came close last year after a poor first half of the season and have since strengthened their squad.

Playing style: PSG began the season well, employing only one striker, Patrice Loko, and a five-man midfield in which Brazilian front men Rai and, more particularly, Leonardo came into spaces created by Loko. Leonardo, later troubled by injuries, notched up seven goals in the first half of the season, to Loko's four. This strategy, essentially based on a solid defence which went unbeaten in the first eight league games of the season, no longer paid dividends following injury to France goalkeeper Bernard Lama. Strengths: Leonardo in good enough form to reclaim and keep his place in the Brazilian team preparing to defend the World Cup in France next year. Some promising young players coming into the squad like midfielder Jerome Leroy and defender Didier Domi.

Weaknesses: Despite his good form, Leonardo is recovering from flu and injury and not at his fittest. Lama no longer a guaranteed secure last line of defence as he was in Euro 96 and the first seven league games this season before cartilage surgery. An aging centre-back pair in Alain Roche and Paul Le Guen. A lack of goals from Loko and the erratic form of Dely Valdes. Distracting off-the-field dispute with England's Arsenal over future of teenage prodigy Nicolas Anelka.

Motivation: The league title which they let slip from their grasp last season. PSG have made it clear everything else comes second behind the bid for the championship. Anxious to show their worth after last week's first leg of the European Super Cup when they were hammered 6-1 at home by Juventus.
